BitTorrent对比主流DePIN项目，用户、产品与销毁

BitTorrent最大的优势，是现成的用户和网络基础。其累计网络地址超过 5.39亿，客户端累计安装超过 20亿次，BTFS节点超过 200万个，存储规模超过 800 PB。相比从零积累用户的Web3存储项目，BitTorrent更有机会把原有用户转化为存储、带宽和链上服务的使用者。

BitTorrent首期销毁约 21.62万亿枚BTT，占总供应量约 2.18%，当时价值约 760万美元。

业务产生收入 → 市场回购BTT → 转入销毁地址 → 永久退出供应

我看了看与同类项目有什么不同的地方
1 / Filecoin的FIL主要通过Gas费和存储惩罚销毁，但网络同时存在代币发行
2 / Arweave没有常规销毁，主要依靠固定供应上限维持稀缺性
3 / Theta的燃烧机制更多作用于TFUEL，而不是THETA本身
4 / Storj虽然有回购安排，但回购代币不一定永久退出流通。

相比之下，BTT的逻辑更加直接，BitTorrent业务收入增长，推动BTT回购，最终通过永久销毁减少供应。

当然，如果这套机制能够延续，那就是是形成一条更清晰的闭环，用户使用服务、业务获得收入、收入回购BTT、销毁减少供应。

这也是BTT相较其他去中心化存储及DePIN代币，最值得关注的差异之一。

$LITE CEO interview on demand, counterparty + financing risk:  

- "CFO of $GOOGL came on and reported capex going up Y/Y, we expect hyperscalers for report an increase in capex in earnings. 

Based on what we see, we see their spend going up."

- "The purchase agreements we have, to a large degree, are noncancellable."

- The difference between Lumentum and companies like $AVGO, "we are not as dependent on AI datacenter buildout going forward"

There's a conversion between electrical products to optical products" creating structural demand. 

Q: When do you see able to see yourself having more inventory? (catching up to surge in demand)

- When we look at demand, there is "no end in sight" 

TLDR:

Financing risk and demand aren't equally distributed across AI supply chains. But markets are just selling everything off together. 

As for photonics in specific, I said this before, but  increasing optical content per XPU + CPO/NPO adoption keeps going up so we'll likely see sector spend go up, even if aggregate capex goes down.

There's the usual "no end to demand in sight" commentary, but $LITE does have capacity commitments into 2029 now... and are negotiating for 2030. (with new information that most of which are likely hyperscalers + non-cancellable) 

So doesn't quite sound like it's all over for the AI trade, especially photonics.

I can't give advice on what others should do but from what I'm seeing from $AAOI revenue ramp, it looks something like this from disclosed capacity. 

-> $858M Q1 2027
-> $1.29B Q2 2027
-> $1.62B Q3 2027
-> $1.89B Q4 2027
-> $2.14B Q1 2028

They're sitting on $6.8B MC right now. I'd be very impressed if they do $7.5B exit annualized revenue run rate in 2027 off 40% gross margins and markets assigned them the same valuation. 

And judging from $LITE making capacity agreements into 2030-2031... I don't quite think demand stalls out after 2027-2028.  

Anyway, lot of execution risk obviously, but H1 2027 inflection point is pretty close, so I'm personally waiting.

Last time I've seen "It's all over" type posts was... 3 months ago during the situational awareness liquidation. 

And... 3 months ago before that... with Iran tensions + Oil + Helium + LNG fears/pricing. 

And... few months ago before that. I'm sure everyone remembers Deepseek back in like 2025

Each one had genuine risks, with rate hikes/margin liquidations to oil prices + supply disruption. And now financing/credit markets. 

Not trying to downplay the risks but haven't seen it materialize in the companies I'm tracking (eg. optical sector) given counterparty types + sector visibility + architectural shifts in 2027-2028.

For example in this $LITE CEO interview, the guy said there hasn't been any order cancellation/delays given rate hikes. 

But obviously neocloud sector that uses heavy debt leverage might be different. 

I've seen that the general sentiment was a recovery after midterms in 2 weeks, I'm not the type to give predictions like that. We'll see

Directionally bullish on certain sectors of AI supply chain like memory/photonics, but everything was sold off indiscriminately, even if they're not exactly the same trade.

Last major $SIVE disclosure was 100M CW DFB laser capacity Q4 2027. And a new foundry partner (that makes 2 including Win Semi).

Expected $JBL revenue coming in H1 2027 (with lasers for Jabil's 1.6T LRO scaling up H2 2027).

There's channel checks along the way like CIOE where Sivers was engaged with Chinese pluggable makers + laser ASPs being raised.

70mW/100mW ranges were the most tight to Chinese pluggable makers, which was surprising.

Biggest industry read through was $LITE selling out into 2029, making agreements for 2030, and having hyperscalers pay for capacity expansion for 2031. 

I don't think anyone has enough information to do any sort of accurate modeling for $SIVE like you can for $AAOI given they don't release product breakdown + capacity targets by quarter.

The 200mW NPO lasers Sivers is sampling is likely different ASP than your 70mW lasers shipped to pluggable makers. And your custom CPO lasers are different pricing too. 

Like all sampling/qualification players from $AEHR to $AAOI back in 2025, usually the risk/reward comes in whether qualifications convert and what new customers they have, which is always a risk. 

In a bull case, if $SIVE comes online with 300m laser supply (2:1 implied ratio, already has "tremendous" supply online from likely US fab) during a structural shortage.  

Pluggable players like $JBL, 6 other vendors.  

$GFS as the reference design laser for their CPO/NPO platform. 

Your minor players vendors like $POET, $AEVA and other players end up scaling.

And all the other custom products they hinted they were working on in the past for CPO years back.  

I think the probability that they cook is higher since there's so many ongoing qualifications during a bottleneck. 

We've already seen ownership changes from Swedish investors to US/International retail from $SIVE shareholder disclosures. 

My guess is that trends institutional from retail before US listing next year amid the market correction. 

Think people forgot institutions have already financed their expansion, which was a 700M SEK round 100%+ ago (multiple times oversubscribed). 

And that $SIVE uses primarily external fabs, so it's not the same as a lot of the major financing concerns affecting Neoclouds.

As a researcher, I like to think about what-if scenarios, so let's consider one here: what if there is no more public-key encryption?

Public-key encryption is used in countless ways in our daily lives, including online shopping, banking, and protecting anything we want to keep private from the rest of the internet.

What if the mathematical problems that underpin public-key encryption (factoring, discrete log, lattice problems, decoding of codes) are all easy to solve because of mathematical breakthroughs by artificial intelligence or quantum computers? What happens to internet commerce?

I see two worlds:

1. We rely on trusted intermediaries to send us keys for encryption. There is no more public-key encryption, and all we have is symmetric encryption like AES. In this case, we need trusted third parties to send counterparties dedicated keys for encrypting.

2. A second possibility that I like better relies on hash-based zk-STARK systems to create digital signatures that depend only on the hardness of hash problems.
In this world, you could still have payment systems and internet commerce for sending payments, but you'll need to solve the challenge of easy, direct encrypted channels between counterparties.

> we could still ultimately do Lattice stuff for accounts, wallets, etc. through a precompile if it is proved to be AI-secure

The ideal route to support everyone's cryptography is imo through 8288. You make whatever signature you want locally, then STARK it, and then it gets included through the stark aggregator machine. Don't need any calldata onchain. Ethereum can then never add a new precompile again.

Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.
